content.value_statement: Azure Messaging SDK failures can be hard to diagnose across languages and services. This skill guides Event Hubs and Service Bus troubleshooting with SDK fixes, logging steps, and service checks.
actual_capabilities: Maps common Event Hubs and Service Bus errors to causes and fixes.
Provides guidance for Python, Java, JavaScript, and .NET SDKs.
Explains logging setup for Azure SDK and AMQP diagnostics.
Guides checkpointing, lock renewal, batching, and client reuse troubleshooting.
References Azure MCP tools for namespace, health, monitor, and documentation checks.
Lists network checks for firewalls, ports, WebSockets, and private endpoints.
limitations: Does not create Event Hubs or Service Bus resources.
Does not perform cost analysis or capacity planning.
Needs user-provided errors, SDK version, and resource context for precise guidance.
Cannot access Azure resources unless connected MCP tools and permissions are available.

use_cases.title: Debug SDK Connection Failures
use_cases.description: Diagnose AMQP errors, timeouts, authentication failures, and WebSocket fallback needs in messaging clients.

use_cases.title: Investigate Message Processing Issues
use_cases.description: Analyze lock loss, checkpointing delays, batch limits, and client lifecycle problems during production incidents.

use_cases.title: Prepare Support Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Collect the right SDK version, logs, namespace health, and configuration details before filing an issue.

prompt_templates.title: Identify an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: I am using Azure Service Bus. Explain what this error means and list the first checks I should make: [paste error].

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Connection Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me troubleshoot an Azure Event Hubs client that cannot connect. My SDK language is [language], version is [version], and the error is [error].

prompt_templates.title: Review Message Processing Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why my messaging consumer stops processing. Include checks for locks, prefetch, checkpointing, retry settings, and client reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step incident runbook for intermittent Azure Messaging failures across SDK logs, Azure health, network checks, and remediation decisions.

output_examples.input: A Python Service Bus receiver raises MessageLockLostError during long processing.
output_examples.output: Likely causes include lock expiry, link detach, or slow processing. Recommended actions include lock renewal, shorter processing work, and network stability checks.

output_examples.input: A Java Event Hubs consumer loses ownership while instances scale out.
output: Explains that ownership changes can be expected during load balancing.
Checks whether churn continues after scaling stabilizes.
Recommends reviewing checkpoint frequency and DEBUG logs.

output_examples.input: A JavaScript client cannot connect through a corporate firewall.
output_examples.output: The skill checks AMQP ports, suggests WebSockets over port 443, and reviews proxy or SSL interception symptoms.

best_practices: Start with the exact SDK, version, error text, and entity type.
Use managed identity or RBAC where possible, and avoid sharing secrets in prompts.
Validate service health and network access before changing application logic.
anti_patterns: Pasting full connection strings, SAS keys, or access tokens into prompts.
Creating one messaging client per operation instead of reusing clients.
Treating transient AMQP disconnects as permanent failures without checking retry behavior.

faq.question: Which Azure services does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Event Hubs and Azure Service Bus SDK troubleshooting.

faq.question: Which SDK languages are included?
faq.answer: It includes Python, Java, JavaScript, and .NET guidance.

faq.question: Can it fix authentication failures?
faq.answer: It can guide checks for connection strings, SAS tokens, RBAC roles, and managed identity setup.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on troubleshooting existing SDK, network, and service behavior.

faq.question: Does it need access to my Azure subscription?
faq.answer: Direct checks need connected Azure MCP tools and permissions. Without them, it can still guide manual troubleshooting.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
